prompt:
Write a police officer's crash report narrative (about 150 words). Collision type: hit while turning left in Houston, Texas. The claimant was a driver and reported back strain. Refer to people as Driver 1, Driver 2 or Passenger. No names, no dates. (Internal reference C-1450; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury is plausible for a crash like this one.
- Photos confirm some details, but there are no independent witnesses.
- It is not clear whether all of the damage came from this impact.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text: Driver 1 was operating a sedan northbound on a Houston city street and was making a left turn at an intersection when the front of the vehicle was struck by a pickup truck, Driver 2, which was proceeding straight through the intersection. Driver 1 reported pain in the lower back and said the force of the impact pushed the body against the seat and steering wheel. A Passenger was seated in the front right position and was also present in the sedan at the time of the collision, a fact confirmed by the investigating officer and by statements from both drivers. No independent witnesses were located at the scene, so the account rests on the parties involved. Photographs taken at the scene show damage to the front bumper, the driver-side headlamp, and the hood of the sedan, along with a crushed right front fender on the pickup. Driver 1 is listed as the named insured on the policy covering the sedan. The officer found no prior damage to the sedan in the vehicle records or in statements given. Because the photographs show damage to several areas, it is not clear at this stage whether all of the visible damage resulted from this single impact. The reported back complaint is consistent with the mechanics of a side impact of this kind.
